L203: Company Description
L204: FO is a licensed manufacturer of light commercial vehicles (Transit, Custom, and Courier models)
L205: and passenger cars (Puma model) on behalf of U.S.-based FMC for the European market and
L206: independently manages the production and sale of Ford heavy-duty trucks for the Turkish and
L207: export markets, with total annual production capacity of 746,500 vehicles at year-end 2023. The
L208: company is also the exclusive distributor of all Ford models in Turkiye under a licensing agreement
L209: with FMC.
L210: FO reported revenue of TRY411.9 billion (equivalent to about €11.9 billion) in 2023, of which 73%
L211: was from international sales. It operates the Golcuk, Yenikoy, and Eskisehir plants in Turkiye, and
L212: the Craiova plant in Romania. The group is equally owned by FMC and Koc Holding, who both own
L213: 41% of its equity. The remaining 18% capital is free float on the Turkish stock exchange.
L214: Our Base-Case Scenario
L215: Assumptions
L216: -
L217: Real GDP growth of 3.0% in Turkiye in 2024-2025 and of 0.7% and 1.3% in the eurozone.
L218: -
L219: Average exchange rate increasing to TRY35.0 per U.S. dollar in 2024 and TRY41.3 in 2022, from
L220: 24.7 in 2023; and $1.09 per euro in 2024 and $1.14 in 2025, from $1.08 in 2023.
L221: -
L222: Turkish core inflation of 55.8% in 2024 and 27.3% in 2025, from 53.8% in 2023.
L223: -
L224: European light vehicle sales rising by 0%-2% in 2024 and 2025 after the 19% growth in 2023.
L225: -
L226: FO's vehicles sold to increase by about 13% to 691,000 units in 2024 and 4.5% to 723,000 units
L227: in 2025 following the capacity expansion at Yenikoy and Craiova.
L228: -
L229: Revenue growth of 80% in 2024 and 42% in 2024, driven by volume growth and lira devaluation.
L230: -
L231: Adjusted EBITDA margin declining to about 7.7% in 2024 and 6.8% in 2025 from 11.7% in 2023
L232: owing to a less favorable pricing environment across Europe and Turkiye and a progressive
L233: dilutive impact from more EV models in the sales mix.
L234: -
L235: Adjusted capex to sales to stay elevated at about 5.2% in 2024 and 4.9% in 2025 as the
L236: company continues to fund its capacity expansion and EV model launches. This translates into
L237: planned total capex net of capitalized development costs of about TRY38.9 billion in 2024 and
L238: TRY52.0 billion in 2025.
L239: -
L240: Dividends of about TRY27.1 billion in 2024 and TRY30.4 billion in 2025, from TRY18.4 billion in
L241: 2023 and in line with the company's minimum payout ratio of 50%.
L242: -
L243: No acquisition or share buybacks.
L244: -
L245: Reported debt figures and the Craiova deferred purchase consideration to increase in Turkish
L246: lira terms in line with our lira devaluation assumption. We estimate that about 87% of the
L247: company's debt structure will remain denominated in hard currency.

L475: Liquidity
L476: We assess FO's liquidity as adequate based on a sources-to-uses ratio of 1.2x over the 12 months
L477: started Jan. 1, 2024. Our assessment includes the successful placement of its unsecured notes of
L478: up to $500 million and €435 million available under its capex loan facility in Romania signed in
L479: March of this year. FO's high amount of short-term debt maturities and lack of long-term

L483: committed revolving credit facility are the main limitations for a stronger liquidity assessment.
L484: Principal liquidity sources for 2024 include:
L485: -
L486: About TRY15.2 billion of cash on the balance sheet on Dec. 31, 2023;
L487: -
L488: Cash FFO of about TRY63 billion;
L489: -
L490: About TRY16 billion received from the up to $500 million planned bond issuance; and
L491: -
L492: About TRY15 billion available under the €435 million capex loan facility in Romania.
L493: Principal Liquidity Uses for the same period include:
L494: -
L495: Short-term debt maturities of about TRY33.8 billion;
L496: -
L497: Working capital investments of TRY8.6 billion;
L498: -
L499: Additional intra-year working capital swings of up to TRY2 billion;
L500: -
L501: Unstressed reported capex of about TRY46.3 billion--we estimate the company could reduce
L502: this amount by at least 15% in a stress scenario; and
L503: -
L504: No committed dividend distributions under a potential stress scenario, compared with TRY27.1
L505: billion in our unstressed base case.
L506: Covenants
L507: FO is subject to a financial covenant under its loan agreements with the European Bank for
L508: Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the International Finance Corporation (IFC), which
L509: stipulates that the group's consolidated reported net debt to EBITDA should not exceed 3.5x. This
L510: covenant is tested semi-annually on June 30 and December 31 of each year. The €435 million
L511: unsecured capex loan facility in Romania is also subject to a 3.5x reported net debt-to-EBITDA
L512: limit, based on the EBITDA generated by the FO Romania entity and debt at this level only. The
L513: planned bond issuance of up to $500 million is not subject to financial covenants.
L514: We expect comfortable headroom under the 3.5x consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA covenant
L515: requirement of the EBRD and IFC loan agreements in the next 12 months, and that FO will adjust
L516: the drawings of its Romania capex loan facility according to the EBITDA growth of the FO Romania
L517: entity, such that it maintains adequate headroom under the local covenant.
L518: Environmental, Social, And Governance
L519: Environmental factors are a negative consideration in our credit rating analysis of FO because it
L520: faces tight fuel efficiency and emissions targets in its main export European market (73% of 2023
L521: sales). We view the group's ability to meet regulatory standards in Europe as in line with that of
L522: many of its peers based on its portfolio plans.
L523: The company's electrification plans are driven by those of its key industrial shareholder and
L524: manufacturing partner, FMC, which targets to offer an all-electric fleet of vehicles in Europe by
L525: 2035 and to introduce new PC and CV electric models in 2024. FMC is also committed to achieving
L526: carbon neutrality no later than in 2050, and no later than 2035 in Europe.
L527: Overall, we believe that consumer acceptance of FO's EV products will be a key credit factor for
L528: assessing its competitive advantage, alongside its ability to maintain sound profitability on those
L529: products.
